observed_behavior: Native host worktree paths had no supported swarm enrollment operation; the coordinator created unbound parent-root standby chats.
expected_behavior: A native isolated checkout can be recorded at its exact physical path and bound to its verified worker.
causal_mechanism: Session creation was ordered after numbered-pool allocation, while native creation did not accept that arbitrary existing checkout. Bookkeeping only allocated numbered paths and could not enroll native roots.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A bookkeeping subsystem constrains the physical identity supplied by an independently owned host lifecycle.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Native creation returns a different valid checkout root; forcing a second path prevents truthful association.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Recorded membership preserves the verified host checkout identity without taking over its physical lifecycle.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Enroll canonical registered same-repository roots under a fenced owner; reject foreign/user/conflicting roots and retain host roots outside numbered-pool reuse/deletion.

applicability_conditions: The host owns native worktree creation and returns an independently selected physical checkout path.
known_non_matches: Existing numbered-pool provisioning remains valid for callers using that provisioning lifecycle.
confirmation_evidence: Source inspection found no existing-root admission operation.
Focused real Git/PostgreSQL proof enrolls an external root, binds its worker and preserves its physical checkout after release and clear.
regression_proofs: tests/swarm-worktrees.integration.test.ts: host worktree enrollment preserves native paths, fences owners and never recycles host checkouts
